decisions.question: Stream identity representation: collision-safe reserved label, native non-label dimension, or staged combination? If native, define storage, query/aggregation, vector matching, duplicate-series, remote-read, /series, label APIs and legacy clients, plus missing/invalid Entity fallback.
decisions.resolution: Decided for the current phase. Every series generated from OTLP or native OTAP carries the ordinary reserved label __otel_resource__, whose value is the hash of the associated logical Resource identity. Use this label rather than a new hidden or native identity dimension. The label participates in stored series identity and is representable through existing duplicate detection, queries, aggregation, vector matching, /series, label APIs, remote read, HTTP and legacy clients. It is an identity carrier, not descriptive metadata enrichment; retaining it does not violate 'metadata ignored by default'. Hashes are lookup and candidate encodings, not substitutes for complete canonical Resource identity and complete-content comparisons. Without usable EntityRefs, use today's explicit compatibility identity: service.name, service.namespace and service.instance.id, preserving absent-versus-empty distinctions. This is a clearly labelled compatibility fallback, not a universal OTel Resource-identity claim. With EntityRefs, hash the authoritative structured identity: each Entity's type; exact typed ID key/value pairs; Entity grouping and set membership; raw Resource attributes not associated with an Entity, which remain identifying; and all required typed content, without stringification. Description-only attributes do not participate. A key that is an ID for one Entity remains identifying even if another Entity uses it only as a description key. Schema URL context is preserved separately and is not silently folded into an identifying attribute. Malformed EntityRefs and duplicate same-type EntityRefs cause atomic rejection of the affected batch or transaction: no fixed-triplet fallback and no samples, metadata/index prefix, WAL prefix or committed-work counters. Adding, removing or changing valid EntityRefs may intentionally change the Resource and series identity; do not reinterpret it as an ordinary descriptive content update.
decisions.limits: Scope metadata may still be retained and queried, but Scope identity does not distinguish otherwise identical streams in this phase. This is a current-phase limitation, not a claim of complete Scope-injective stream identity and not a universal rule that Scope can never matter. Metric properties and data-point attributes remain distinct logical stream dimensions under existing translation semantics.

decisions.question: Association cardinality and conflicts: one owner per series/kind/time or several legitimate owners? For contradictory same-time and late/multi-writer claims, reject the transaction or retain samples with an explicitly unresolved association, and what is the replay result?
decisions.resolution: Decided. For current Resource, Scope, Metric, Resource-schema and Scrape relations, allow at most one active owner for a series and metadata kind at a particular time. Multiple independent domains can coexist; competing owners within one domain must not become implicit multiple enrichments. Genuine future many-to-many relations require explicitly named relation semantics rather than implicit exceptions. Conflict matrix: same owner, same complete content and same effective time is an idempotent observation with no new version, extending observation bounds only when needed; same owner and effective time with different complete content rejects the whole transaction atomically; same series/kind/effective time with different owners rejects the whole transaction atomically; same owner/content at another point in its existing epoch extends observation bounds only with no version; different content at a new effective time inserts an ordered actual version whose predecessor ends exclusively at that time; a different owner at a new effective time inserts an ordered membership band whose predecessor ends exclusively at that time; input addressing discarded or truncated state is rejected or exposes explicit truncation, never inventing exact history or resurrecting discarded state. Rejection publishes no samples, metadata/index prefix, WAL prefix or committed counter, and previously committed state is unchanged. Do not commit samples while retaining an unresolved contradictory association; no quarantine or conflict subsystem is selected. Effective time, not arrival time, defines validity and temporal order. Observation of the content or owner already applicable at that time only extends observation bounds. Backfilled actual content or membership changes insert ordered history and affect only the resulting band. Backfilled content equal to an immediate successor may coalesce that redundant successor while preserving both observation histories. Observation bounds never move across an actual content or membership change point. A/B/A produces a new A epoch after B; it does not extend the first A epoch through B. Content histories and membership histories follow those rules independently. No exact historical answer may be claimed from discarded or ambiguous observations. Arrival time, map iteration, writer name, receiver and OTAP batch ID are never precedence rules. Validate against committed state before publication and publish accepted transactions atomically. The same initial state plus a fixed ordered committed log must reproduce exactly the same history, memberships, observation bounds, truncation and errors on replay. Unrelated commit orders are not required to be commutative or to produce an arbitrary identical winner. Rejected transactions are not committed-log entries. Committed replay must not manufacture versions, memberships, metadata-only blocks or additional bounds. Flush, compaction or snapshot restore plus replay must reproduce the same retained state. Transport acknowledgements do not imply exactly-once delivery. No distributed transaction or coordination requirement follows.
decisions.limits: Source/provenance is deliberately excluded from the generic one-owner answer and remains decision 5; this decision does not settle Source as single-valued or multi-valued. Decision 3 (unknown, clearing and expiry) and all other open decisions remain unanswered. No quarantine or unresolved-conflict-retention subsystem is selected.

decisions.question: Unknown, clearing and expiry: which producer/API operation clears content or ends membership, is there an explicit lease or expiry separate from observation, and what does each query return for absent, unknown, cleared, truncated and coalesced states?
decisions.resolution: Decided. Observation is not expiry. Preserve typed present/null, absent, explicitly cleared, unknown, truncated and coalesced states distinctly. Keep three axes independent rather than collapsing them into a single found boolean: content (which value or assertion applies at a time), association applicability (which owner applies to the series or domain at that time) and history coverage (what retained evidence remains available to answer). Value and knowledge states: present means an authoritative assertion supplies the complete typed value; null means a typed null was explicitly supplied and is present, not absent or unknown; absent means an authoritative complete content assertion does not contain the key; cleared means an explicit deletion or tombstone says a previously meaningful value or association no longer applies; unknown means there is no applicable trustworthy assertion, observation or retained history from which to answer; truncated means an answer might have existed but retained coverage is explicitly incomplete and is not a successful current-value lookup; coalesced means examples or ranges were deliberately merged under policy and exact intermediate changes are not claimed. Missing keys in partial Resource descriptions mean unknown for that source, not absent or cleared. Partial input leaves unknown fields unresolved. Only authoritative complete content or an explicit policy can assert omission as absence. Provably redundant equal-successor coalescing is lossless and must not be relabelled lossy coalescing or truncation. A version-count cap alone is not a complete memory bound or a semantic definition of these states. Explicit key clear and explicit association termination are separate operations, usable in metadata-only transactions, replayed deterministically and durable across lifecycle operations. Explicit key clear: the old value ends at the clear's inclusive EffectiveFrom and the preceding version is exclusive immediately before it; no current value is promoted or returned; historical content before the clear remains readable; reappearance creates a new version; clearing one key does not clear unrelated keys; clearing every Resource attribute does not itself remove Resource identity or its series associations; other members and metadata domains are unaffected; repeated equivalent clears are idempotent observations under decision 2. Explicit association termination is represented as an actual membership successor: the previous owner ends at the termination time exclusively; later queries report the series as unassociated using the selected explicit semantics; later reassociation creates a new band; owner content and other series members are unaffected; owner history is not deleted by one member's departure. Equal-time owner-versus-owner or owner-versus-termination disagreement remains a decision-2 atomic conflict; the whole affected transaction rejects without publishing a prefix. Current metadata has no general wall-clock lease. No implicit expiry: do not infer expiry from ObservedFrom or ObservedUntil, missing observations or missed scrapes, sample staleness, process restart, close, replay, flush, compaction, rollout or wall-clock time, or arrival order or transport retry. Latest content remains applicable until an actual successor, explicit clear or policy-based retention. A disappearing series does not implicitly clear its Resource or Scope context. Close and reopen does not age metadata. No generic lease or TTL subsystem is selected for this phase; a future authoritative protocol expiry must be explicit domain-authorized validity state, not receiver timeout behavior or time.Now() construction. Queries expose absence and uncertainty rather than pretending these states are ordinary empty labels. Query behavior: existing queries and vector matching ignore metadata by default; unknown, absent, cleared and truncated states synthesize no fake promoted label; series lacking usable context survive unfiltered enrichment; positive value filters match only an applicable present value and absent, cleared or unknown do not silently equal an empty-string value; selecting a missing or cleared state requires an explicit state predicate rather than a magic value under an ordinary label matcher; range evaluation uses the applicable stable validity band and does not select one clear or reappearance arbitrarily for the entire range; one input series contributes at most once across clear, reappearance and association transitions; historical diffs express before/after state changes explicitly rather than encoding a clear as old->; reverse filtering still requires a common overlap of content validity, membership validity and query range; metadata-only clear, absence, truncation and history paths read zero sample payloads. No applicable association, an applicable owner with the key absent, a key explicitly cleared, and no exact answer because coverage is unknown or truncated must not all collapse to the same not-found response. Retention and coalescing change evidence coverage, not the meaning of retained facts: expose history truncation and, where representable, earliest retained coverage; preserve observation and association coverage limits; preserve a separate marker for lossy coalescing if introduced under policy; queries requiring discarded history report unknown or truncated, not absent or cleared; immutable older parts must not resurrect cleared values or associations; lossless equal-successor coalescing preserves combined observation ranges. Transactions and lifecycle: validate every change before publication; rejected clear or termination changes publish no samples, metadata/index prefix, WAL prefix or committed counter; metadata-only changes fabricate no samples or sample time coverage; replay and compaction preserve change order, tombstones, applicability, observation bounds and coverage flags exactly; arrival order cannot overwrite a newer committed value with an older one; close/reopen or newer immutable-part recovery cannot resurrect cleared state; partial multi-source descriptions preserve independent assertions and provenance and do not merge, clear or reconcile Resources from matching names alone.
decisions.limits: Decision 3 does not decide Source cardinality (decision 5), PR99 grammar (decision 6), typed HTTP or cursor schema (decision 7), coexistence (decision 8) or admission and retention budgets (decision 9). Exact PR99 syntax for selecting unknown, absent or cleared states and exact JSON/HTTP response encoding are deferred to decisions 6 and 7; this decision fixes only the semantic distinctions and query behavior they must preserve. No generic lease or TTL subsystem is selected for this phase. Current-phase limit: the incumbent has no typed-null, tombstone, association-termination, completeness/provenance or state-specific response representation; the accepted clear, termination, typed-state and partial-input clauses remain explicit non-passing target cases rather than being inferred from current prototype behavior.
